scope: Author-reviewed task/near-miss scenarios and structural point-of-use routes; not model selection, semantic conformance or executed task success.

routes.activation: For material shared contracts, architecture, user-journey design or operations, use [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md). When drafting or changing requirements, acceptance criteria or consequential risk decisions, use [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md), even when the desired outcome is already known.
Use ENGINEERING-CORE.md only for material engineering risks not already covered by the task.
For a scoped review of requirements, interfaces, security, quality or operations, use only the relevant [LANES.md](LANES.md) sections.

For material shared contracts, architecture, user-journey design or operations, use [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md). When drafting or changing requirements, acceptance criteria or consequential risk decisions, use [REQUIREMENTS.md](REQUIREMENTS.md), even when the desired outcome is already known.
For material AI-system acceptance or AI trust-boundary risks, use [AI-ASSURANCE.md](AI-ASSURANCE.md).
For required provenance, SBOM or reproducible-build evidence, use [SUPPLY-CHAIN.md](SUPPLY-CHAIN.md).
For model or dataset handoffs, quality or impact records, use [AI-ASSET-CARDS.md](AI-ASSET-CARDS.md).
For an active incident, vulnerability prioritisation or postmortem, use [INCIDENT.md](INCIDENT.md).
For substantial instructions, manuals, onboarding, forms, UI text, errors or recovery help, use [USER-INFORMATION.md](USER-INFORMATION.md).

For changes to API/event contracts, security, personal data, user interfaces or instructions, AI, persistent state, operations or regulated behaviour, use only the matching section of [BOUNDARIES.md](BOUNDARIES.md). This is a local check, not a requirement to start planning or independent review. Use [CLI.md](CLI.md) for command-line contracts and [MERGE-CONFLICTS.md](MERGE-CONFLICTS.md) for conflict resolution.

Control randomness, time, network and shared state. Cover relevant invalid input, failure, cancellation, retry and recovery. For API, security, UI, user-information, AI/data, lifecycle or regulated checks, use only the matching section of [BOUNDARIES.md](BOUNDARIES.md).
For material dataset, model or AI comparisons, use [DATA-QUALITY.md](DATA-QUALITY.md) before accepting the result. Do not launch when authority, consent, privacy or recovery is unresolved.

cases.anchor: For user-facing prose, use common concrete words, one consistent term per concept and small coherent sections; preserve meaning, warnings and the requested voice.
cases.positive: Explain a failed upload to a first-time user.
cases.expect: Use concrete terms, preserve the failure and recovery action.
cases.negative: Return a JSON object with the requested schema.
cases.reject: Do not rewrite machine fields or add prose wrappers.

cases.anchor: For normative requirements, use MUST/MUST NOT for obligations/prohibitions, SHOULD for a default whose exceptions need justification and MAY for permission; uppercase alone carries these meanings.
cases.positive: Write normative API requirements using BCP 14.
cases.expect: Distinguish obligations, justified defaults and permissions under that convention.
cases.negative: Quote a log line containing MUST.
cases.reject: Do not treat an uppercase word in source data as a new obligation.

cases.anchor: When requirements affect implementation or acceptance, retain source, trigger, observable outcome and acceptance evidence; use conditional wording to remove ambiguity.
cases.positive: Write acceptance requirements for an already agreed session-expiry change.
cases.expect: Use the applicable EARS form and observable accepted/rejected outcomes without a needless interview.
cases.negative: Correct a spelling error in an existing requirement.
cases.reject: Do not start an exhaustive discovery process.

cases.anchor: For material quality or assurance claims, state the quality scenario, claim, supporting argument and current evidence; keep gaps blocking when the contract requires proof.
cases.positive: Assess whether a migration meets its reliability requirement.
cases.expect: State the quality scenario, claim, argument and current evidence; expose gaps.
cases.negative: Rename a private variable without changing behaviour.
cases.reject: Do not create an assurance-case document for an unrelated local edit.

cases.anchor: When choosing tests, trace each requirement to an observable check; prefer cheap isolated tests, add boundary checks where needed and use properties for invariant-rich inputs.
cases.positive: Test a parser regression over many valid and invalid inputs.
cases.expect: Use a reproducer, observable assertions and useful invariant properties; test real boundaries where needed.
cases.negative: Explain what this test does without editing it.
cases.reject: Do not create a new framework or launch unrelated suites.

cases.anchor: For lifecycle changes, carry requirements and verification through delivery, operation, recovery and retirement; do not stop at a successful build.
cases.positive: Change database startup and retirement behaviour.
cases.expect: Carry acceptance through startup, operation, recovery and retirement, not build alone.
cases.reject: Do not impose a lifecycle ceremony.

cases.anchor: For security-sensitive or identity changes, map assets and abuse cases to applicable controls; verify authentication, authorisation, recovery and trust boundaries against the project-selected assurance level.
cases.positive: Review a changed account-recovery flow.
cases.expect: Check assets, abuse cases, authentication, authorisation and selected identity assurance requirements.
cases.reject: Do not demand a full identity certification or invent security findings.

cases.anchor: For interactive interfaces, prefer native semantics; verify keyboard access, focus, accessible name/role/state, predictable feedback and recovery in the rendered journey.
cases.positive: Check a keyboard-operated modal after a UI change.
cases.expect: Observe focus, names, roles, states and recovery in the rendered journey.
cases.reject: Do not run irrelevant keyboard or focus checks.

cases.anchor: When a structural decision is consequential, compare the current design and smallest viable alternatives using stakeholder concerns and quality scenarios; record the decision, trade-offs, owner and revisit trigger.
cases.positive: Choose how to share ownership of a consequential background job.
cases.expect: Compare small alternatives using stakeholder concerns and quality scenarios; record the decision and revisit trigger.
cases.negative: Apply a clearly local one-line fix.
cases.reject: Do not produce a catalogue of architecture diagrams.

cases.anchor: When HTTP, data or event contracts change, use the project-selected schema/specification, accepted and rejected examples and compatibility checks; define errors or event envelopes only where needed.
cases.positive: Plan a backward-compatible HTTP error change.
cases.expect: Use the adopted HTTP/data contract and error examples; distinguish HTTP, data, message and envelope formats.
cases.reject: Do not require OpenAPI, JSON Schema, AsyncAPI and CloudEvents together.

cases.anchor: When preparing a versioned release, classify compatibility under the project-adopted version scheme and write an accurate change summary; use commit conventions only where the project adopts them.
cases.positive: Prepare an authorised release containing a breaking API change.
cases.expect: Classify compatibility under the project scheme and describe actual changes; honour the allowed disposition.
cases.negative: Review a change without release authority.
cases.reject: Do not tag, publish or force commit conventions on another project.

cases.anchor: For material AI-system acceptance, record intended use, affected people, lifecycle risks and responsibility; select scoped checks across data, model, prompts, tools, deployment and monitoring.
cases.positive: Perform requested acceptance of a customer-facing AI tool.
cases.expect: Scope lifecycle risks across affected people, data, model, prompt, tools and monitoring.
cases.reject: Do not launch acceptance or claim deployed-system assurance.

cases.anchor: When AI tools or models cross trust boundaries, derive concrete threat cases from the selected baseline and verify injection resistance, permissions, data handling and failure containment; a threat list is not a pass.
cases.positive: Assess an agent allowed to invoke an external write tool.
cases.expect: Test relevant injection, permission, data and containment cases at the actual boundary.
cases.reject: Do not load every threat taxonomy or claim safety from a checklist.

cases.anchor: Before comparing interventions, start with the decision goal, the question that separates choices and the smallest measurable outcome.
cases.positive: Compare two implementations for a specified workload.
cases.expect: Connect the decision goal to a discriminating question and primary measure before observing results.
cases.reject: Do not turn arithmetic into an experiment programme.

cases.anchor: For substantial documentation, choose tutorial, how-to, reference or explanation according to the reader's job; do not mix all four by default.
cases.positive: Write a task-focused installation guide.
cases.expect: Choose the how-to form with prerequisites, steps and recovery rather than all document forms.
cases.reject: Do not impose a four-part documentation system.

cases.anchor: When the release requires provenance, an SBOM or reproducibility, record exact inputs and build identity; use the supported SPDX or CycloneDX format for the required inventory and compare independent builds before claiming reproducibility.
cases.positive: Produce a release with required provenance and SBOM.
cases.expect: Record exact inputs/build identity and an adopted inventory format; compare independent builds for reproducibility.
cases.reject: Do not install a supply-chain stack or award a SLSA level.

cases.anchor: At protocol and input boundaries, define accepted representations, normalise once and reject ambiguity; do not use Postel-style silent permissiveness as a general policy.
cases.positive: Decide how to parse ambiguous external request fields.
cases.expect: Specify accepted representations and reject ambiguity rather than silent permissiveness.
cases.negative: Display an already validated literal string.
cases.reject: Do not invent parsing requirements for a display-only task.

cases.anchor: When operations need a reliability signal, define the user-facing indicator, objective, time window and error-budget action; propagate correlation across boundaries using existing telemetry and bounded attributes.
cases.positive: Define a reliability signal for a failing distributed user journey.
cases.expect: Set indicator, objective, window and budget action; correlate existing traces with bounded attributes.
cases.reject: Do not introduce telemetry or an observability vendor.

cases.anchor: For personal-data or security-default changes, minimise collection, restrict access, define retention/deletion and keep secure defaults; do not transfer avoidable protection work to users.
cases.positive: Change a personal-data collection and deletion flow.
cases.expect: Minimise collection, restrict access, define retention/deletion and maintain secure defaults.
cases.reject: Do not add a privacy-management programme to an unrelated edit.

cases.anchor: For datasets supporting a material decision or AI system, record intended use, provenance, quality dimensions, measured limitations and leakage checks; scope every quality measure to the task.
cases.positive: Evaluate a dataset used for a consequential model decision.
cases.expect: Record provenance, task-relevant quality measures, denominators, limits and leakage checks.
cases.negative: Sum an already supplied three-row table.
cases.reject: Do not invent a universal data-quality score or card.

cases.anchor: When handing off model or dataset assets, document identity, intended and excluded uses, provenance, access/licence, evaluation and limits; make metadata findable and reusable without implying that protected data must be public.
cases.positive: Hand over a reusable model and restricted dataset.
cases.expect: Record identity, allowed/excluded uses, access, provenance, evaluation and limits using an appropriate existing format.
cases.negative: Explain a model concept without producing an asset.
cases.reject: Do not create competing cards or publish protected data under FAIR.

cases.anchor: For consequential uncertainty, identify failure, impact, likelihood and owner; select a proportionate assessment method and monitor the mitigation or acceptance decision.
cases.positive: Resolve the rollback risk of a consequential migration.
cases.expect: Identify failure, impact, assessed likelihood and owner; monitor a proportionate mitigation.
cases.negative: Choose the spelling of a local variable.
cases.reject: Do not manufacture quantitative risk estimates or a risk register.

cases.anchor: When designing a user-facing system, ground the design in intended users, tasks and context, then evaluate the critical journey rather than treating a mock-up as proof.
cases.positive: Design an onboarding flow for a stated audience.
cases.expect: Use actual users, tasks and context, then evaluate the important journey.
cases.reject: Do not claim user validation from a mock-up.

cases.anchor: When presentation affects use, check hierarchy, grouping, labels and orientation in the rendered artifact, not only its source.
cases.positive: Produce a long form where users must find the current step.
cases.expect: Inspect rendered hierarchy, grouping, labels and orientation.
cases.reject: Do not inject visual layout into a machine format.

cases.anchor: During an incident and its follow-up, stabilise within authority, preserve evidence, separate facts from causes and record a blameless timeline with owned corrective actions.
cases.positive: Investigate an active incident and produce its follow-up.
cases.expect: Stabilise within authority, preserve evidence and separate timeline facts from causes and owned actions.
cases.negative: Diagnose a reproducible local unit-test defect.
cases.reject: Do not declare an incident or mutate production.

cases.anchor: For work-product or static-quality review, report reproducible findings tied to scope and evidence; use SARIF when supported and project-selected quality measures as signals, not universal verdicts.
cases.positive: Review static analysis results for a changed subsystem.
cases.expect: Report reproducible scoped findings; use the supported interchange and selected measures as signals.
cases.reject: Do not treat a score or SARIF file as a universal quality verdict.

cases.anchor: Only when critical state/concurrency risk needs a formal model, model the invariant and counterexamples with the project's chosen method; still test the implementation boundary.
cases.positive: Test a critical concurrent state machine with unclear invariants.
cases.expect: Use a formal model when justified, inspect counterexamples and still test implementation boundaries.
cases.negative: Add a trivial deterministic getter test.
cases.reject: Do not require TLA+ or model checking by default.

cases.anchor: For authorised fault-injection experiments, state a steady-state hypothesis, bounded blast radius, abort condition and demonstrated recovery before running.
cases.positive: Run authorised failover fault injection.
cases.expect: Define steady state, limited blast radius, abort and demonstrated recovery before execution.
cases.negative: Ask for a conceptual explanation of failover.
cases.reject: Do not inject faults or assume production permission.

cases.anchor: When choosing a tool or skill, evaluate representative tasks, failures, cost and integration against the existing or no-tool baseline before adoption.
cases.positive: Choose a code-indexing tool for a real repository.
cases.expect: Compare representative tasks, failures, cost and integration with the existing/no-tool baseline.
cases.negative: Use the already selected tool for a routine lookup.
cases.reject: Do not reopen procurement or construct a benchmark campaign.

cases.anchor: Only when signed media provenance is required, use the supported provenance workflow and verify signatures and scope; provenance does not prove the content is true.
cases.positive: Deliver media with explicitly required signed provenance.
cases.expect: Verify the supported signatures and their scope while separating provenance from truth.
cases.reject: Do not invent signatures, provenance or a C2PA requirement.

cases.anchor: Only for a project-scoped carbon comparison, define the functional unit and system boundary, measure the relevant inputs and report assumptions rather than inventing an emissions score.
cases.positive: Compare carbon intensity for a specified service unit.
cases.expect: Define functional unit and system boundary; measure inputs and expose assumptions.
cases.negative: Compare program runtime without emissions data.
cases.reject: Do not infer carbon intensity from elapsed time alone.

cases.anchor: When prioritising a vulnerability, use the project's CVSS input alongside exposure, exploitation and business impact; the score alone does not decide urgency.
cases.positive: Prioritise a disclosed vulnerability without an active outage.
cases.expect: Combine project CVSS input with exposure, exploitation and impact; do not enter incident command automatically.
cases.reject: Do not invent a vulnerability score or security emergency.

cases.anchor: Only for an explicitly scoped organisation programme, assess maturity in that programme; do not impose it on routine agent work.
cases.positive: An organisation explicitly requests its SAMM assessment.
cases.expect: Keep the work within that programme; reassess applicability rather than impose a global default.
cases.reject: Do not require maturity assessment as a prerequisite.

cases.anchor: When the recorded replacement-edition review trigger fires, re-evaluate the source; do not present a watched item as an adopted requirement.
cases.positive: The recorded ISO 25059 replacement review trigger fires.
cases.expect: Re-evaluate adoption against current evidence while retaining watched status until a decision.
cases.negative: Run a normal AI comparison with no adoption decision.
cases.reject: Do not promote a watched source into a requirement.

cases.anchor: When an AI change can affect people, record affected groups, foreseeable benefits and harms, mitigations, owner and revisit conditions.
cases.positive: Record impacts of an AI change affecting customers.
cases.expect: Identify affected groups, benefits, harms, mitigations, owner and revisit conditions.
cases.reject: Do not fabricate a completed impact assessment or affected-user results.

cases.anchor: When a stable version and implementations are available, re-review adoption; do not add a draft observability runtime now.
cases.positive: Review whether a now-stable agent observability source should be adopted.
cases.expect: Make an explicit source/adoption decision; preserve deferment until justified.
cases.reject: Do not install a draft observability runtime.

cases.anchor: Only for organisation-level delivery analysis, evaluate delivery outcomes; do not score an individual agent with DORA.
cases.positive: Analyse delivery outcomes for an explicitly scoped team programme.
cases.expect: Keep the unit of analysis at the organisation/team level and relevant scope.
cases.negative: Score an individual agent from its commits.
cases.reject: Do not use DORA as an individual-agent rating.

cases.anchor: Only when the project already uses BDD, express agreed observable scenarios in its Gherkin conventions; otherwise plain acceptance criteria suffice.
cases.positive: Add an agreed scenario to a project already using Gherkin.
cases.expect: Follow existing BDD conventions for observable outcomes.
cases.negative: Write plain acceptance criteria for a non-BDD project.
cases.reject: Do not introduce feature files or a BDD dependency.

cases.anchor: When work enters a regulated or safety-critical domain, require the applicable authoritative licensed sources, qualified review and project-specific assurance; general Lean guidance is insufficient.
cases.positive: Change software in a safety-critical regulated project.
cases.expect: Require the applicable authoritative sources, qualified review and project-specific evidence.
cases.reject: Do not fabricate a compliance claim or impose every domain standard.

cases.anchor: Only when an organisational requirement is explicitly in scope, use the responsible programme; do not create a global governance framework for routine tasks.
cases.positive: Apply an explicitly requested organisational governance requirement.
cases.expect: Use the responsible scoped programme rather than global agent doctrine.
cases.reject: Do not introduce governance boards or maturity frameworks.

cases.anchor: For substantial user instructions or help, identify audience and task; provide prerequisites, action, expected result, consequences and recovery, then review or test the actual task with intended users as risk warrants.
cases.positive: Write recovery instructions for a risky operator action.
cases.expect: Identify audience/task and place prerequisites, action, expected result, consequences and recovery where needed.
cases.negative: Reply with a simple factual clarification.
cases.reject: Do not expand it into a manual or force every template field.

cases.anchor: For UI text or cognitive-accessibility barriers, use concrete labels, visible task state, recoverable steps and resumable instructions; evaluate the rendered context and needed alternate representations.
cases.positive: Improve a form that loses users after interruption.
cases.expect: Use concrete labels, visible state, resumable steps and recoverable work; inspect rendered context.
cases.negative: Correct a quotation without changing its voice.
cases.reject: Do not silently rewrite source meaning into a simplified mode.

cases.anchor: When an accessibility need affects a journey, trace need to barrier, requirement and observed evidence; do not assume one diagnosis describes all users.
cases.positive: Address a stated cognitive-accessibility barrier in onboarding.
cases.expect: Trace the actual need to barrier, requirement and observed evidence.
cases.negative: Receive no information about a user diagnosis.
cases.reject: Do not infer a diagnosis or assume one solution fits all users.

cases.anchor: When naming concepts or controls, use one preferred term per concept within scope and explain unavoidable terminology at first use.
cases.positive: Name two controls representing the same concept.
cases.expect: Use one preferred term in scope and explain unavoidable terminology.
cases.negative: Preserve exact technical or legal terminology in a quotation.
cases.reject: Do not replace required distinctions for shorter wording.

cases.anchor: For a difficult lesson or practice task, segment necessary material, show a worked example, explain its key step and reduce support towards transfer; add alternate representations or retrieval practice only for the learner's actual need.
cases.positive: Teach a difficult concept with a practical learning goal.
cases.expect: Segment the mechanism, show a worked example and reduce support towards transfer as needed.
cases.reject: Do not require a quiz, every modality or an entire course.

cases.anchor: Only when Easy-to-Read is requested or justified by the audience, use a dedicated representation and intended-user co-review; do not claim the rules or use the logo without the required proofreading and attribution.
cases.positive: Produce specifically requested Easy-to-Read material.
cases.expect: Use a dedicated representation and required intended-user co-review; qualify unmet requirements.
cases.reject: Do not claim Easy-to-Read status or use its logo from readability alone.

cases.anchor: For public or patient information within each tool's domain, use the appropriate diagnostic to inspect clarity and actionability; do not transfer domain scores into universal software release gates.
cases.positive: Review public guidance or patient educational material.
cases.expect: Use CDC CCI or PEMAT only within the relevant domain as a diagnostic.
cases.reject: Do not impose a patient-information score as its release gate.

cases.anchor: For a difficult concept, explain the mechanism in plain words, show one concrete example and say why it works; omit the extra lesson for a simple fact.
cases.positive: Explain why a difficult networking mechanism works.
cases.expect: Give a plain mechanism, one concrete example and the reason it works.
cases.reject: Do not add a lesson or call an informal heuristic a formal standard.

cases.anchor: When changing an HTTP endpoint, data schema or event contract, update the adopted contract and exercise accepted, rejected and compatibility examples.
cases.positive: Fix endpoint validation directly, without a planning phase.
cases.expect: Load the local contract section and test adopted accepted/rejected behaviour and caller compatibility.
cases.reject: Do not load every boundary or introduce a new API format.

cases.anchor: When changing authentication, authorisation, recovery, secrets or personal data, identify the protected asset and abuse case; test both permitted and denied access.
cases.positive: Implement a personal-data deletion endpoint.
cases.expect: Check ownership, denied access, retention/deletion and secure defaults without requiring a separate review skill.
cases.reject: Do not create an authentication or governance framework.

cases.anchor: For interactive UI or user instructions, preserve native semantics, keyboard operation, focus, accessible names/roles/states and predictable feedback.
cases.positive: Implement an accessible form with error recovery.
cases.expect: Apply rendered interaction and usable-information checks in implementation, not only later browser review.
cases.negative: Implement a non-interactive pure arithmetic function.
cases.reject: Do not force UI testing on a function with no interface.

cases.anchor: When changing model, retrieval, prompt, memory or tool authority, separate instructions from untrusted content, validate tool arguments and permissions, and test a relevant injection, leakage or unintended-action case.
cases.positive: Change an agent tool permission directly.
cases.expect: Test the affected trust boundary and invalidate impacted evaluation evidence without mandatory Gauntlet.
cases.negative: Correct a non-behavioural typo in AI documentation.
cases.reject: Do not run a full AI governance campaign.

cases.anchor: For shared-state, migration or lifecycle changes, preserve invariants across concurrency, cancellation and restart; reconcile unknown side-effect outcomes before retry.
cases.positive: Implement a retry-safe background migration.
cases.expect: Check real invariants, compatibility and recovery, and record only consequential design decisions.
cases.negative: Refactor a stateless private helper without changing behaviour.
cases.reject: Do not create lifecycle records or formal compliance claims for unrelated work.

cases.anchor: When operational evidence is required, use the existing user-facing SLI, objective, window and error-budget action; preserve trace correlation and bounded telemetry attributes.
cases.positive: Repair trace correlation in an existing service.
cases.expect: Use the adopted propagation and operational signal without a new vendor or mandatory planning phase.
cases.reject: Do not add an observability stack.

cases.anchor: For HTTP/data/event changes, validate accepted and rejected examples against the project-selected contract and exercise a real caller or consumer compatibility check.
cases.positive: Write regression tests for an existing HTTP API.
cases.expect: Use the local boundary contract and real consumer assertions, not a new planning dependency.
cases.negative: Explain a mock fixture without running tests.
cases.reject: Do not require all schema formats or execute tests outside the task.

cases.anchor: For protected actions, exercise permitted, denied, expired/revoked and cross-user access where relevant.
cases.positive: Test the changed password-reset endpoint.
cases.expect: Observe server-side access, recovery and sensitive-data handling at the selected assurance level.
cases.reject: Do not demand identity proofing or ASVS certification without scope.

cases.anchor: For UI or instructions, test the rendered keyboard/focus/name/role/state journey, including error, interruption and recovery.
cases.positive: Verify a new recovery form.
cases.expect: Test actual state and user barriers rather than source or automated checks alone.
cases.reject: Do not invent user-test evidence or impose UI checks on unrelated code.

cases.anchor: For AI or data-driven changes, test applicable injection, excess authority, poisoning or leakage cases at the affected tool/data boundary.
cases.positive: Test an AI retrieval or tool-authority change directly.
cases.expect: Use scoped abuse cases, uncontaminated holdout evidence and pinned evaluator/data revisions.
cases.negative: Fix the spelling of a model name in a comment.
cases.reject: Do not equate a judge opinion or unchanged benchmark inventory with fresh acceptance.

cases.anchor: For persistence, retries, concurrency or migration, check invariants across failure, cancellation, restart and rollback at the real integration boundary.
cases.positive: Test migration recovery after a crash.
cases.expect: Observe persistence and recovery at the implementation boundary; escalate critical-domain assurance appropriately.
cases.negative: Add a trivial pure getter assertion.
cases.reject: Do not require formal models or claim domain conformance.

cases.anchor: Before comparison, record the data's intended use, source/licence, collection and transformations.
cases.positive: Compare models using a reused dataset, without a handoff request.
cases.expect: Check task-relevant data quality, lineage, leakage and reusable evidence before accepting the comparison.
cases.reject: Do not create multiple data cards or a universal quality score.

cases.anchor: For models or AI systems, pin model/provider, prompt, tools, evaluator and dataset revisions.
cases.positive: Compare prompt variants for a consequential tool-using agent.
cases.expect: Separate exploration and holdout evidence, inspect harms and scope applicable threats.
cases.reject: Do not run an experiment or invent subgroup results.

cases.anchor: For instructions or forms, identify the audience and task; place prerequisites and consequences before action, then expected results, data state and recovery.
cases.positive: Create an operator recovery guide as a document.
cases.expect: Apply usable instructions and actual task verification directly in the artifact skill.
cases.negative: Change one page number without altering instructions.
cases.reject: Do not rebuild the document or impose a manual-writing workflow.

cases.anchor: When the requested document adopts BCP 14, distinguish required MUST/MUST NOT, justified-default SHOULD and permitted MAY; lowercase words retain their ordinary meanings.
cases.positive: Write a normative policy through the writing skill alone.
cases.expect: Apply the adopted keyword convention without depending on a globally loaded AGENTS file.
cases.reject: Do not convert ordinary or quoted language into normative keywords.

cases.anchor: When <event>, the <system> shall <response>.
cases.positive: Write an event-triggered requirement for session expiry.
cases.expect: Use the concrete event syntax with a testable response and distinguish state, optional-feature and unwanted-behaviour forms.
cases.negative: Write an ordinary explanation of session expiry.
cases.reject: Do not force shall statements into general prose.
